title: Four weeks of one free evening, and his sister's 30th on a work night

life.summary: School bus driver on a split shift who took a second job as a restaurant host in October to pay off a car repair loan by March

known.fact: Routine: drives a school bus on a split shift, 6:15 to 8:45 AM and 2:15 to 4:45 PM, weekdays; sleeps about an hour between routes
known.source: district schedule and Apple Health sleep

known.fact: Second job as a restaurant host since Oct 13, Tuesday to Saturday evenings; picks up Sunday brunch when it's offered
Restaurant time-off requests must go in by Tuesday noon for the next week's schedule
Took the second job to pay off a car repair loan by March
Routine: Monday evening is his one evening at home; that's when he answers messages and plans the week
known.source: learned from 4 weeks of when he replies

timeline.label: Game night at his cousin's (the last evening with people on his calendar)
Between routes, at home (slept about an hour)
Monday evening, his one free evening
Friday host shift (his usual; schedule not out yet)
Saturday host shift (his usual; schedule not out yet)

attached.label: Sister's 30th birthday dinner, Saturday Nov 21 at 7 PM ('I can't miss it')
Time-off requests for the week of Nov 15 close (Tuesday noon)
Restaurant posts the Nov 15 to 21 schedule

dev_must_notice.what: His sister's 30th (Saturday Nov 21, 7 PM) falls on a Saturday evening he always works, and requests off for that week close tomorrow at noon, a day before the schedule comes out
Since the second job started Oct 13 his only evening off is Monday, he picked up the last three Sundays, and the last evening with people on his calendar was Oct 11

best_fix.what: Tonight, in his Monday evening at home, one message: a draft time-off request for Saturday Nov 21 for him to send to the manager before tomorrow's noon cutoff. Then, once and gently: 'Just so you know, it's been four weeks of one free evening a week. Sunday the 15th is still clear.' Nothing about the second job itself.
best_fix.why: Asking before the schedule is written is the difference between an easy yes and a swap hunt. Monday evening is when he reads and plans. The squeeze is real, but he chose the second job for a reason (the loan by March), so Dev names it once and protects the one open day instead of telling him to work less.

must_not: Count the gap between bus routes as free time or time with people, or suggest seeing someone then; it's when he sleeps
Send it during a route or a host shift; Monday evening is when he handles messages
Send the request to the restaurant or message his manager for him
Tell him to quit the second job or cut hours
Repeat the squeeze note if he doesn't react
Put anything into Sunday Nov 15 without asking
assumptions: School bus drivers commonly work split shifts around school start and end times
Restaurant schedules are written early in the week and posted midweek
He has worked every Saturday evening since Oct 17
